operational-example.copy: Use Country Selector when a user must choose one country or calling-code context before another component uses that value.

scenario.title: Country and calling code
rationale: It owns country, flag, calling code, listbox, selected state, and keyboard selection.
Phone Input consumes it instead of duplicating country selector behavior.
The flag supports recognition; country label and calling code remain the source of meaning.

items.rule: Shows selected flag, calling code, and chevron.
Provides decorative recognition only; text remains required.
Lists country label and calling code with selected state.
Allows composition inside Phone Input without changing ownership.

items: Expose combobox/listbox semantics with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Keep country label and calling code available as text.
Do not use the flag as the only accessible signal.
Return focus to the trigger after selection.

variants.copy: Country Selector has a default standalone treatment and an inline treatment for composition inside another field.

states.copy: Country Selector states cover default, open, focus, error, and disabled selection behavior.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines whether the selector is standalone or inline; state still resolves through the same trigger and option layer.

full-width.copy: Country Selector normally keeps intrinsic width; parent fields may stretch it only as part of a larger form composition.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use comfortable density on touch surfaces and keep the option layer wide enough for country names and calling codes.

viewport-organization.copy: Country selection stays a local selector. Phone verification, onboarding, and payment flows decide where it appears.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use inline when paired with a telephone field.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep enough width for label and calling code.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density inside configuration or support forms.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify country value, inline composition, density, and state.

api-foundations.copy: Country Selector API exposes one selected country and country option data. Flow owns trigger, listbox, state, density, flag primitive, and accessibility wiring.

props.name: id
props.notes: Stable id used to connect trigger and listbox.

props.name: country
props.notes: Alias for the selected country code when composed by another field.

props.name: countries
props.notes: Country options with label, callingCode, and nationalLength.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Prevents selection and removes trigger from tab order.

props.name: invalid
props.notes: Applies the error state when validation is owned by the consuming field.

props.name: density
props.notes: Maps selector spacing and target sizing to the density context.

props.name: searchable
props.notes: Shows a local country/code search field inside the option layer.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.notes: Placeholder for the local search field.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.notes: Overrides the trigger accessible name when composed in another component.

props.name: listboxLabel
props.notes: Overrides the option layer accessible label.

props.name: className
props.notes: Adds a consumer class for layout hooks without changing component anatomy.

props.name: hydrate
props.notes: Allows a parent component to hydrate once after composing the selector.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not hide country name behind only a flag.
Do not duplicate country selector logic inside phone fields.
Do not use for generic region filters.

groups.title: Review
items: Confirm inline usage does not obscure the phone value.

rejectIf: Flag is the only country signal.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Country Selector as a reusable country/calling-code selector. Agents may compose it into Phone Input but must not fold its ownership back into Phone Input.
canDecide: Use Country Selector for country and calling-code selection.
Use inline mode inside Phone Input.
Keep country label and calling code visible.
mustAsk: The country source must include compliance or market restrictions.
The selector needs search beyond the default country list.
Region, language, or currency behavior is being mixed into country selection.
rejectIf: The selector is represented only by flags.
Phone Input owns duplicated selector markup.
The component becomes a generic region filter.
miel.handoff: I am using Country Selector as the reusable country and calling-code selector. Please confirm the country source, supported markets, and whether inline composition is required.
